# 9.2 Biome Hazard & Encounter Guides

# A. The Southern Desert & Sunken Necropolis (Rows 13–16, Cols 10–19)

  • Environmental Hazard (Ambient Heat & Quicksand):
  • Morning (06:00–09:00): 85°F, tolerable footing.
  • Midday (09:00–12:00): 115°F, DC 12 Con save per hour for heavy armor wearers.
  • Afternoon (12:00–15:00): 150°F, ground traversal without shade causes 2d6 fire damage per 10 minutes.
  • Quicksand Traps: Hexes (11, 15) and (12, 13) require DC 14 Perception to spot; failing players sink 5 ft per round (DC 15 Athletics/Dexterity to escape).
  • Creature Threats:
  • Air Elementals & Dust Devils (CR 5): Hexes (12, 14), (11, 16), (13, 14). Air elementals use Whirlwind (DC 13 Str, 3d8+2 bludgeoning + hurled 20 ft). Flanking in swirling sand inflicts the Blinded condition (DC 13 Con save).
  • Giant Scorpions (CR 3): Hex (15, 15). Burrow under dunes, attacking with surprise claw grapples and lethal sting poison (4d10 poison, DC 12 Con half).
  • Dust Mephits (CR 1/2): Swarm travelers in sandstone crevices; Blinding Breath (DC 10 Dex) and Death Burst (blinded 1 minute).
  • Tactical Discoveries:
  • Colossal Dune Ribs (14, 14): Ancient leviathan skeleton casting dense, cool shadows. Provides complete thermal shelter up to 140°F.
  • Alabaster Steps (15, 14): Inscribed with pre-loop celestial pictograms explaining how the Arcanist inverted the souls of the Angel and Devil.

# B. The Dwarven Crags & Granite Peaks (Rows 4–7, Cols 13–20)

  • Environmental Hazard (Scree & Sheer Altitude):
  • Vertical cliffs require DC 13 Athletics or climbing kits. Steep gravel scree gives Disadvantage on Dexterity checks and acrobatics.
  • Creature Threats:
  • Stone Giants (CR 7): Hexes (12, 6), (14, 6), (15, 6).
  • Oreg the Carver (12, 6): Solitary, contemplative hermit carving loop murals. Non-hostile if approached respectfully or offered uncut gems.
  • Terrace Bowlers (14, 6): Territorial giants rolling 200-lb granite boulders down gorge chutes (DC 15 Dex save or 4d10 bludgeoning and knocked prone).
  • Mountain Wyvern (CR 6): Hex (14, 4). Nests on jagged pinnacles. Pike the Barbarian can pacify or tame this beast with a DC 15 Wisdom (Animal Handling) check using the Zephyr Bone Whistle.
  • Tactical Discoveries:
  • Cold-Iron Veins (15, 5): Natural veins of anti-magical ore. Dwarven miners will smelt 2 anti-fiend piercing spearheads in 30 minutes if delivered to Hex (15, 7).
  • Abandoned Sentry Redoubt (11, 5): Stone cliffside fortification stocked with 10 heavy crossbow bolts, dry dwarf bread, and a spyglass granting +2 to spot incoming aerial threats.

# C. The Glacial Frostpeaks & Icy Chasm (Rows 6–12, Cols 16–20)

  • Environmental Hazard (Permafrost & Sub-Zero Cold):
  • Extreme cold (20°F down to -15°F near Rimefang's lair). Characters without cold weather gear make DC 10 Con saves every hour or gain 1 level of Exhaustion.
  • Glacial Crevasses: Hidden beneath fresh powder (DC 13 Perception); drop 40–60 ft (4d6 to 6d6 bludgeoning).
  • Creature Threats:
  • Winter Wolves (Ice Wolves) (CR 3): Hex (18, 9), (17, 7). Pack hunting tactics with Frost Breath (4d8 cold damage, 15ft cone, DC 12 Dex half). Keen Hearing and Smell gives Advantage on Perception.
  • Ice Trolls (CR 5): Hex (18, 7), (19, 12). Regenerate 10 HP per round unless attacked with Fire or Acid.
  • Tactical Discoveries:
  • Glacial Meltwater Moraine (15, 9): Sub-zero rushing torrent. Drinking pure water grants Advantage on Constitution saves against heat exhaustion for 2 hours.
  • Mammoth Tusk Cairn (19, 9): Ancient nomad monument holding an ivory hunting horn that grants +10 ft movement speed when blown.

# D. The Deep Weirwood Forest & Northern Canopy (Rows 2–7, Cols 5–14)

  • Environmental Hazard (Dense Brambles & Disorienting Mists):
  • Dense conifer and oak canopy blocks 90% of direct sunlight, providing natural solar shelter up to 15:00 PM.
  • Creature Threats:
  • Owlbear (CR 3): Hex (7, 4). Aggressive nesting predator guarding hollow ancient redwood where Item 8 is hidden.
  • Displacer Beast Pack (CR 3): Hex (9, 7). 2 stealthy predators utilizing Displacement (all attacks have Disadvantage until hit).
  • Wild Wolves (CR 1/4): Hex (10, 2). Pack of 4 den wolves.
  • Tactical Discoveries:
  • Fey Fairy Ring (9, 2): Circle of glowing luminescent toadstools. Spending 10 minutes meditating inside restores one 1st-level spell slot (once per character per loop).
  • Ranger's Hidden Cache (6, 3): Hollow tree stump containing 1 longbow, 20 fletched arrows, and 2 flasks of herbal anti-toxin.

# E. The Sword Coast & Western Ocean (Rows 9–16, Cols 1–5)

  • Environmental Hazard (Gales & Crashing Surf):
  • 35-knot winds reduce flying speed by 10 ft unless flying with the wind. Crashing surf requires DC 12 Athletics to swim without being battered against razor barnacles.
  • Creature Threats:
  • Sahuagin Baron & Raiding Patrol (CR 5 & CR 1/2): Hex (4, 11), (3, 12). Utilize Blood Frenzy (Advantage on melee attacks against targets that don't have full HP) and command trained reef sharks.
  • Giant Octopuses (CR 1): Guard the sea caves of Hex (4, 11) using 15-foot reach tentacle grapples.
  • Tactical Discoveries:
  • Barnacle Reef Shoal (3, 9): Submerged reef sheltering giant clams containing lustrous pearls worth 100 GP each (material component for Identify).
  • *Wreck of the Wavecrest*** (4, 12): Beached merchant vessel holding 150 ft of silk rope and a brass underwater lantern.

# 10. Capstone Boss Lethality Architecture & The Four Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs)

# 10.1 The Philosophy of "Razor-Thin" Lethality in a Time Loop

In standard tabletop campaigns, high-mortality encounters risk campaign derailment. In the Beregost Time Loop, however, death carries zero permanent consequence—the party awakens at 06:00 AM at the sundial. This allows the DM to tune both wilderness encounters and capstone bosses to Deadly+ (CR 13–15) lethal thresholds.

# The Resource Attrition Engine

  1. No Long Rests: The loop spans strictly 12 hours (06:00 to 18:00). A long rest requires 8 hours, making resource recovery mid-cycle mathematically impossible.
  2. Short Rest Time Taxation: A 1-hour short rest consumes 8.3% of the party's entire temporal budget, risking the 12:00 PM aerial cutoff or 15:00 PM surface heat scorch.
  3. The Wilderness Gauntlet (Resource Taxing):
  • Hexes are populated with encounters that drain spell slots, Barbarian Rages, and Monk Focus points if tackled recklessly.
  • The Learning Curve: On initial loops, players stumble into Air Elemental basins or quicksand, arriving at the boss depleted and suffering total party wipes within 2 rounds.
  • The Mastery Curve: Players learn which hexes to avoid, which shortcuts bypass guardians, and which 2–3 counter-items MUST be gathered on the single execution loop.
  1. The Razor-Thin Boss Victory:
  • Even with all counter-items and meta-knowledge, the bosses possess massive HP pools, high AC, and devastating physical burst damage.
  • Items neutralize the boss's instant-wipe "gimmicks" (e.g. dragon's 80ft aerial kiting, mummy's incurable rot, rakshasa's limited magic immunity, storm giant's party-wide lightning arcing), reducing the battle from an impossible wipe to a tense, high-stakes tactical duel where victory is just barely achieved.

# 11. The Architecture of Rewards, Meta-Progression & The Genie Protocol

# 11.1 The Strict Reset Boundary: What Persists vs. What Resets

To preserve the tension and high-stakes puzzle nature of the time loop, nothing persists across dawn resets except the players' memories and their milestone level-ups:

Asset / AttributePersists Across Resets?Mechanical Rule & Flavor Justification
Player Memories & KnowledgeYES (100%)The 5 PCs are the sole entities retaining temporal continuity. True Names ("Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak", "Ravana-Zul"), somatic/vocal rites (the Inversion Touch & Celestial Reversal Chant from Boss 2's Golden Tablets), codes (7-3-9-1), passwords ("Khazad-Mor"), and NPC schedules remain in player memory.
Milestone Level-UpsYES (Permanent)Milestone levels are awarded upon defeating each Capstone Boss (Lvl 7 → 8 → 10 → 11). Overcoming impossible planar threats elevates the party's combat mastery and spell access across loops.
Soul-Imprints / Blessings / SigilsNO (Strictly None)No NPC, deity, or genie retains a "soul-imprint" of the party across resets. All divine blessings, Genie Wishes, and NPC alliances must be triggered in-loop using memorized True Names and leverage.
Physical Items, Boss Hearts & WeaponsNO (Vanishes at 06:00)Gold, forged weapons, arrows, Canopic Hearts, and physical relics revert to their dawn positions across the map. However, if a boss's reward is pure memorized knowledge (like Boss 1's Genie True Name, Boss 2's Inversion Rite, or Boss 3's Rakshasa True Name), the party never needs to re-fight that boss on future loops!
The Djinni's Wish & Nimbus CloudNO (Fades at 06:00)The Elemental Wish and the One-Time Nimbus Cloud granted by Zephyrus reset at dawn. To use them on a new loop, the party must visit Hex (11, 12) and speak his memorized True Name ("Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak").
NPC & Boss DeathsNO (Resurrects at 06:00)All slain monsters, raiders, and bosses wake up unharmed at dawn.

# 11.2 The Five Categories of Memorized Knowledge Rewards (The True Progression)

# 1. True Names & Planar Invocation Protocols

  • The party learns and memorizes the ancient secret formulas to command planar beings. Once memorized, players never need to re-fight the original boss to invoke them on later loops:
  • From Boss 1 (Rimefang, Hex 17, 10): The party memorizes Djinni Zephyrus's True Name ("Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak") and his 3-note wind cadence. Speaking his True Name at the Aerie of the Four Winds (Hex 11, 12) compels him by ancient elemental law to grant 1 Elemental Wish + 1 One-Time Nimbus Cloud move (15 min/hex in one move only) without re-fighting Rimefang!
  • From Boss 2 (Akh-en-Amon, Hex 12, 16): The party memorizes the Somatic Inversion Touch & Celestial Reversal Chant from the Golden Alabaster Tablets. They can perform this somatic/vocal rite directly at Ash Grove (Hex 7, 6) to heal and recruit the True Angel without ever returning to the southern desert!
  • From Boss 3 (Lord Ravana, Hex 10, 6) & Town Clues (Maya / Corin): The party memorizes Lord Ravana's Infernal True Name ("Ravana-Zul") and his 06:15–06:45 AM Cobbler's Lane disguise schedule. On the Final Loop, they ambush and bind him right in Beregost (Hex 8, 10) at 06:15 AM (0 hexes traveled!), forcing him to surrender his Blessed Piercing Quiver & Monocle, and aid the party at the Spire (Hex 6, 8) at 17:30 PM!

# 2. Milestone Level Progression (Levels 7 → 11)

  • Boss 1 Defeated (Adult White Dragon) → Level 8:
  • Monk/Barbarian gain ASI/Feat; Druid gains 4th-level spells (Blight, Polymorph, Conjure Woodland Beings); Fighter gains subclass enhancements; Rogue gains ASI.
  • Boss 2 Defeated (Mummy Lord) → Level 10:
  • Druid gains 5th-level spells (Greater Restoration, Mass Cure Wounds); Rogue gains Reliable Talent; Barbarian gains Brutal Critical; Fighter/Monk gain tier-3 combat milestones.
  • Boss 3 Defeated (The Rakshasa) → Level 11:
  • Fighter gains 3 attacks per Action; Druid gains 6th-level spells (Heal, Sunbeam); Rogue/Monk/Barbarian gain tier-3 capstones.
  • Boss 4 Freed (Storm Giant) → Unlocks 17:30 PM Supercell Hurricane & Campaign Finale!

# 3. Social "Checkmates" & Instant Leverage

By discovering NPC crimes, secrets, and grief during previous loops, the party can bypass hours of social navigation in seconds:

  • Alderman Durlag (06:15): Knowing his clerk is forging blackmail ledgers allows the party to instantly demand the release of the cold-iron transport wagons at 06:15 instead of waiting until 08:30.
  • Constable Renwick (07:00): Inspecting the North Gate ledger reveals that 'Lord Aurelius' cast no shadow when entering the settlement at dawn.
  • Lord Ravana / "Aurelius" (06:15): Knowing he prepares his Deva disguise in Cobbler's Lane (Hex 8, 10) at 06:15 AM and knowing his True Name ("Ravana-Zul") lets the party bind him in Beregost before he ever steps outside the North Gate.
  • Young Kaelen in Beregost (Hex 8, 10): Visiting his boarded-up room at Feldepost's Inn at dawn (or under the church crypts in the afternoon) and reciting Bram's code 7-3-9-1 convinces him to immediately hand over the completed Chronomancy Tuning Fork and his Calibration Cipher.
  • The Circle of Druids & True Angel (Hex 7, 6): Reciting the memorized Inversion Swap Chant and performing the Somatic Inversion Touch from Boss 2's Golden Alabaster Tablets halts the druid binding ritual and heals the True Angel without needing the physical stone tablets.

# 4. The Wilderness Hazard Blacklist (Resource Preservation)

Every fight avoided in the wilderness saves HP, spell slots, and rages for the capstone bosses. Through trial and error, the party maps the Hazard Blacklist:

  • Hex (12, 14): Greater Air Elemental Basin (Avoid to save 6d8 bludgeoning damage).
  • Hex (11, 15): Quicksand Sinkhole (Avoid to save 2nd-level spell slots).
  • Hex (14, 6): Stone Giant Boulder Bowling (Avoid to save 4d10 bludgeoning damage).
  • Hex (18, 7): Regenerating Ice Troll Crevasse (Avoid to save Gwen's fire spells).

# 5. The Relic Arsenal Coordinates & Guardian Bypasses

The party discovers that nearly every counter-item guardian can be bypassed without fighting using meta-knowledge:

  • Dwarven Aerie Sentinel (Hex 14,7): Speak the memorized dwarven password "Khazad-Mor" (learned from the runestone in Boss 1's chasm) to claim the Drake-Bane Censer peacefully.
  • Winter Wolves (Hex 18,9): Throw fresh meats from Tobias's bakery to distract the pack; snatch the Boots of the Winter Strider with zero damage taken.
  • Mother Owlbear (Hex 7,4): Pike blows the Zephyr Bone Whistle to pacify her maternal aggression; retrieve the Blessed Quiver peacefully.
  • Desert Obelisk Elementals (Hex 13,14): Speak Auran prayers learned from the Frozen Wind-Stele at (17,10) or Djinni Zephyrus at (11,12); elementals bow and yield the Scarab of Solar Resurgence.

# 11.3 The Genie Protocol (Zephyrus the Cloud-Lord)

# How the Party Unlocks the Genie (Boss 1: Dragon Slaying)

  1. At Glacial Frostpeak (17, 10), the party slays Rimefang (Adult White Dragon) in the 60×60 ft 6-Pillar Frost Vault for the first time.
  2. In Rimefang's frozen hoard, they shatter the permafrost casing around the Frozen Wind-Stele of Zephyrus (T14–U15)—an ancient sapphire-and-basalt slab inscribed with Celestial/Auran runes (note: Zephyrus himself is not physically in the dragon cave; he resides inside his Brass Lamp at Hex 11, 12!).
  3. The unsealed Wind-Stele and Glacial Treasure Chart reveal:
  • Zephyrus's physical Brass Lamp rests at the Aerie of the Four Winds (Hex 11, 12)—a wind-scoured alabaster mesa rising high above the southeastern dunes.
  • His True Name is "Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak" (accompanied by a specific 3-note wind cadence).
  1. When invoked at his Brass Lamp at Hex (11, 12), Zephyrus grants them 1 Active Wish and 1 One-Time Nimbus Cloud move (15 min/hex), and the party achieves Milestone Level 8!

# How the Party Re-Summons the Genie on Subsequent Loops (Using Memorized True Name Only!)

  1. When time resets to 06:00 AM, the party awakens at the sundial. Their Level 8 status and memories persist, but Zephyrus himself has reset with zero memory or soul-imprint of the party.
  2. The Shrine Location: His corporeal vessel resides at The Aerie of the Four Winds (Hex 11, 12) (4 hexes SE of Beregost).
  3. The True Name Invocation:
  • At Hex (11, 12), the party climbs the alabaster steps and speaks his memorized True Name: "Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak!"
  • Bound by the immutable laws of the Elemental Plane of Air, speaking a Djinni Prince's True Name at his vessel overrides the frost-seal for that day and compels him to honor the ancient pact—even though he does not remember the party!
  • Zephyrus manifests and grants two boons for that day:
  1. One Elemental Wish: Party-wide resistance/immunity to a chosen element for the day:
  • Option A (For Boss 2 Mummy Lord): Party-wide Resistance to Necrotic Damage.
  • Option B (For Boss 3 Rakshasa / Afternoon Heat): Wish of Frozen Heart (Party-wide Immunity to Ambient Solar Scorch & Fire/Radiant Resistance).
  • Option C (For Boss 4 Storm Giant): Party-wide Resistance to Lightning & Thunder Damage.
  1. One-Time Nimbus Cloud Traversal (15 min/hex in ONE move only): Zephyrus conjures a roaring Nimbus Cloud that carries the entire party across the map at 15 minutes per hex (4 hexes/hr) for ONE continuous point-to-point move only, ignoring surface heat and midday thermal turbulence. As soon as the party steps off the cloud at their destination hex, the cloud dissipates!

# 12.2 The Endgame "Golden Loop" 12-Hour Route Puzzle (Sessions 12–13)

By the end of the campaign (Level 11), the players know what must be done to defeat The Singing Devil (CR 16) atop the Spire of the False Angel (Hex 6, 8) at 17:30 PM and shatter the Chronocite Bone before 18:00 PM. However, because nothing persists across resets except their memories and level-ups, every physical ally and item has reset at 06:00 AM!

# Step 1: How Player Memory Prunes the 6 Boss Sites Down to 4 Stops

To survive the 17:30 PM confrontation at Hex (6, 8), the party needs Six Victory Conditions active on the Final Day:

  1. The Burning Book Unlocks the Spire Portal (Hex 7, 10 → Hex 6, 8):
  • The Problem: The colossal adamantine gates of the Spire of the False Angel (Hex 6, 8) are sealed by searing white-hot celestial flame wards that deflect all mundane and spell attacks.
  • The Origin & Mystery: The party carried the Burning Book (a living solar grimoire) on their initial predawn arrival into Beregost before Loop 0, but dropped it in the dark barleyfields of Hex (7, 10). The dropped book ignited a vast wildfire. While Beregost is protected by stone irrigation ditches and plowed firebreaks, traversing or searching the burning field on foot is impossible (3d6 fire damage / 10m, blinding smoke).
  • The 05:45 AM Aerial Breakthrough: During the predawn 05:45 AM causal flight with the True Angel, the party flies over Hex (7, 10) before the fire has spread. Looking down in the twilight, they spot a tiny fire—a single campfire-sized spark where the book first struck the stone furrow! Spotting this exact aerial landmark allows the party to pinpoint and retrieve the Burning Book on subsequent loops, which unlocks the Spire gates!
  1. Lord Ravana Bound & Town Evacuated (Hex 8, 10):
  • How Memory Solves It in 15 Mins (0 Hexes): From Maya, Corin, and Boss 3's Resonance Ledger, the players know "Aurelius" is Lord Ravana, that he prepares his disguise in Cobbler's Lane (Hex 8, 10) at 06:15 AM, and that his Infernal True Name is "Ravana-Zul". The party ambushes him right in Beregost at 06:15 AM and speaks his True Name—binding him without a lengthy wilderness chase, forcing him to surrender his Blessed Piercing Quiver & Monocle, refrain from inciting Archdruid Faelan, and report to the Spire (Hex 6, 8) at 17:30 PM! Simultaneously, the party gives Captain Rebecca and Sister Althea advance warning to prepare town defense and shelter, and teaches Elorion the counter-melody.
  1. Tempest Lord Otheus Unchained (Hex 5, 11 via Hex 4, 10):
  • Why They Must Visit: Otheus is physically chained underwater at Hex (5, 11). Without him, the 17:30 PM orbital solar beam deals 100d10 unavoidable radiant damage.
  1. Young Kaelen's Chronomancy Tuning Fork (Hex 8, 10):
  • Why They Must Visit: The physical Chronomancy Tuning Fork is required to shatter the Chronocite Bone in the escapement gear after the Singing Devil falls. The Town Team collects it directly from Young Kaelen boarded up in Room #4 at Feldepost's Inn during dawn (06:00–06:15 AM) by providing proof of the loop!
  1. Djinni Zephyrus's Wish & One-Time Nimbus Cloud (Hex 11, 12):
  • Why Boss 1 (Hex 17, 10) Is Skipped: The party already memorized Zephyrus's True Name ("Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak") from Boss 1. Flying to his vessel at Aerie of the Four Winds (Hex 11, 12) and speaking his True Name grants 1 Elemental Wish (Wish of Frozen Heart for afternoon 175°F heat immunity) AND the One-Time Nimbus Cloud (15 min/hex in ONE move only)—without re-fighting Rimefang!
  1. The True Angel Healed & Recruited (Hex 7, 6):
  • Why Boss 2 (Hex 12, 16) Is Skipped: The party already memorized the Somatic Inversion Touch & Celestial Reversal Chant from Boss 2's Golden Alabaster Tablets. They never need to return to the Southern Desert (Hex 12, 16); they simply visit Ash Grove (Hex 7, 6), perform the memorized somatic touch, and recruit the True Angel to meet them at the Spire (Hex 6, 8) at 17:30 PM!

# Step 2: Why Naive Routes Fail (The Movement Math Puzzle)

The players must clear Four Key External Objectives—The Burning Book (Hex 7, 10), West Coast (Hex 5, 11, deadline 09:45 AM), North Ash Grove (Hex 7, 6, deadline 11:30 AM), and Southeast Aerie (Hex 11, 12)—and unite at the Spire of the False Angel (Hex 6, 8) by 17:30 PM:

  • ❌ Why Walking Together Fails: The full circuit (8,10 → 7,10 → 5,11 → 7,6 → 11,12 → 6,8) is ~20 hexes long (20+ hours on foot), and the druids execute the True Angel at Hex (7, 6) at 11:30 AM every loop by default while the raiders blow up Hex (5, 11) at 09:45 AM!
  • ❌ Why Flying All Day Together Fails: Early-Morning Flight (2 hexes/hr = 30 min/hex) only lasts 2 hours (06:00 AM – 08:00 AM) before rising heat grounds flying mounts, AND the Zephyr Bone Whistle Gryphon carries at most 2 players (the other 3 must walk at 1 hex/hr)!
  • ✅ The Winning Insight (Coordinated Morning Split + Genie's One-Time Nimbus Cloud):
  • Because every non-combat checkmate on the Final Loop uses memorized True Names, Ciphers, and Somatic Rites, the party splits at 06:15 AM (right after binding Ravana in Beregost) to beat both morning deadlines (09:45 AM West & 11:30 AM North) and uses Zephyrus's One-Time Nimbus Cloud (15 min/hex) to reunite everyone at the Spire (Hex 6, 8) before 17:30 PM!

# 12.3 The True Final Boss: The Singing Devil in the Angel's Body

  • Identity: The ancient Archdevil trapped in the radiant, feathered body of the True Angel. It communicates exclusively through eerie, resonant singing and choral incantations. It wields both unholy hellfire and blinding radiant celestial wrath.
  • CR / Target Level: CR 16 (XP 15,000; PB +5) Large Fiend (in Celestial Deva Form), Lawful Evil | Level 11 Campaign Climax.
  • Official D&D 2024 (5.5e) Stat Block:
  • AC: 19 (Natural Armor & Unholy Aegis) | HP: 245 (22d10 + 110) | Speed: 30 ft., fly 90 ft. (hover)
  • Ability Scores: STR 24 (+7), DEX 18 (+4), CON 20 (+5), INT 18 (+4), WIS 18 (+4), CHA 22 (+6)
  • Saves: Dex +9, Con +10, Wis +9, Cha +11 | Skills: Deception +11, Insight +9, Perception +9, Performance +11
  • Resistances: Cold; Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from nonmagical attacks
  • Immunities: Fire, Necrotic, Poison | Condition Immunities: Charmed, Exhaustion, Frightened, Poisoned
  • Senses: Truesight 120 ft., Passive Perception 19 | Languages: All, Telepathy 120 ft.
  • Traits:
  • Discordant Resonance: Any non-fiend within 30 ft has Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration.
  • Legendary Resistance (3/Day): If it fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.
  • Magic Resistance: Advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects.
  • Actions (D&D 2024 Format):
  • Multiattack: Makes three attacks: two with its Radiant Hellfire Greatsword and uses one Choral Dirge.
  • Radiant Hellfire Greatsword: Melee Attack Roll: +12, reach 10 ft. Hit: 21 (4d6 + 7) Slashing plus 14 (4d6) Radiant or Necrotic damage.
  • Choral Dirge: Wisdom Saving Throw: DC 19, creatures within 60 ft. Failure: 22 (4d10) Psychic/Thunder damage and Frightened for 1 minute.
  • Chronocite Ray (Recharge 5–6): Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 19, 120-ft line. Failure: 55 (10d10) Force damage and Incapacitated until start of next turn.
  • Bonus Actions:
  • Angelic Wing Feint: Disengages and flies up to 30 ft without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
  • Reactions:
  • Parrying Chorus: Trigger: Attacked in melee. Response: Adds +5 to AC against that attack.
  • Legendary Actions (3/Round):
  • Choral Blast (1 Action): Ranged Attack Roll: +11, range 60 ft. Hit: 14 (2d8 + 5) Thunder damage.
  • Planar Teleport (2 Actions): Teleports up to 60 ft to unoccupied space.
  • Harmonic Rupture (3 Actions): Constitution Saving Throw: DC 19, 20-ft radius. Failure: 28 (8d6) Radiant/Hellfire damage.
  • Location: The Spire of the False Angel Hex (6, 8) (Western Sea Cliffs) — sympathetically linked to The Beregost Clocktower Belfry Hex (8, 10) at 17:30 PM.
  • The Climax Mechanic:
  1. At 17:30, Tempest Lord Otheus (Hex 5, 11, just 3 hexes south on the coast!) unleashes the Category-5 Supercell Thunderstorm over the Western Sea Cliffs, deflecting 85% of the orbital solar beam and dragging the Singing Devil down onto the parapet of The Spire of the False Angel (Hex 6, 8).
  2. The True Angel (in the horned Devil's body), stabilized in the North Forest (Hex 7, 6), flies to Hex (6, 8) to fight alongside the party!
  3. The party must sunder the Singing Devil's celestial wings while the True Angel chants the Inversion Reversal Rite memorized from the Golden Alabaster Tablets.
  4. Upon the Devil's defeat, their souls swap back to their rightful forms. Striking the sympathetic resonance rift with Kaelen's Chronomancy Tuning Fork (or flying with the restored True Angel back to the Beregost Clocktower Belfry Hex 8, 10), the party strikes the Solstice Bell and sunders the Chronocite Bone in the escapement gear before 18:00 PM!
  5. THE TIME LOOP PERMANENTLY SHATTERS!

# Act I: The Shock of Dawn & Beregost Under Siege (Sessions 1–3)

  • Session 1: Loop 0 — The First Day & The 18:00 Cataclysm
  • Events: The party unjams the Clocktower at 05:59 AM and experiences Beregost's Solstice Festival. Meet cheerful Tobias (bakery), Little Maya, Old Jonas (8-line prophecy), Captain Rebecca, Alderman Durlag, and Scribe Vane. Rescue Tom at (8, 11) and interrogate Snirk at (9, 10).
  • Midday Escalation: 09:00 thermal spike (95°F); 12:00 solar scorch (2d6 fire/10m); 15:00 bunker panic (175°F). Party desperately casts Create Water and tries to save civilians in the temple cellar.
  • Climax: 17:59 orbital solar detonation. Total party wipeout. Gears clack.
  • Cliffhanger: 06:00 AM. Dawn Monologue read verbatim.
  • Session 2: Loop 1 — The First Boss Duel & The 11:30 AM Loud Explosion
  • Events: Testing loop causality. At 07:15 AM, the party is approached by "Aurelius the Radiant" (the disguised tiger-headed Rakshasa). He tells them the Angel from their prior campaign was corrupted by a horned fiend in the northern woods and gives them the Crucible Charm to "cleanse" it.
  • The First Boss Battle (Hex 7, 6): The party engages the Horned Fiend (CR 10, 165 HP)! Ensnared by Lord Ravana's Crown of Fiendish Delirium, the True Angel in the Devil's body acts genuinely malicious and attacks the druids and party on sight—only snapping out of his confusion once the Rakshasa (Boss 3 at Hex 10,6) is defeated!
  • The Soul Detonation (Default Every Loop): When defeated by the party or executed by Faelan's druids at 11:30 AM, its celestial soul ruptures in a 70 radiant/fire damage Soul Detonation, wiping out the grove and prompting Old Jonas's 8-line rhyme on the next dawn ("First east to the ice, then south to the sand...").
  • Session 3: Loop 2 — Mapping the Wilderness & The Movement Lesson
  • Events: Venturing east and south to investigate Jonas's rhyme and Bram's thermal readings.
  • The Lesson: Discovering the strict movement rules: 1 hex/hr (60m/hex) on foot and 2 hexes/hr (30m/hex) by air only during the 2-hour dawn window (06:00 AM – 08:00 AM, max 2 riders on the Bone Whistle Gryphon). Stumbling into screening hazards teaches the party to map detours and locate counter-items.

  • Boss Fight: Rimefang grounded on Round 1; Censer negates Frightful Presence; 6 Glacial Pillars provide cover against Cold Breath. Dragon slain!

Invoking Zephyrus at (11, 12) with his memorized True Name for Necrotic Resistance + the One-Time Nimbus Cloud (15m/hex) to hop across the dunes to the Sunken Necropolis (12,16).

# 13. The Capstone Discovery Pipeline & The Bootstrap Paradox

# 13.1 The Capstone Discovery Pipeline: The Sequential Breadcrumb Trail

Rather than confronting players with an overwhelming open sandbox of four omnipotent bosses at Level 7, the campaign employs a sequential investigative discovery pipeline guided by Old Jonas's Four Corners Solstice Prophecy. None of the bosses are "temporal anchors"—instead, defeating each boss yields the memorized True Name, sacred somatic ritual, or ally needed to unlock the next step of the mystery!

# Step 1: The False Capstone Trap (Loop 1)

  • The Misdirection: Posing as "Aurelius the Radiant" at 07:15 AM, the tiger-headed Rakshasa convinces the party that the "horned archdevil" in the northern forest is causing the solar collapse.
  • The Outcome: The party fights the Horned Fiend (Prelude First Boss). Its death triggers the 11:30 AM soul detonation (or the 18:00 PM wipeout). The loop resets identically. The party realizes: Killing the horned beast did NOT fix the sun—that wasn't the capstone boss at all!

# Step 2: Old Jonas's Prophecy East & Boss 1 (Loops 2–5)

  • The Investigation: The party listens carefully to Old Jonas's Four Corners Prophecy: "First east to the ice, then south to the sand, find the path to stop the devil's hand... Slay the white wyrm for his chart, to claim a wish of frozen heart."
  • The East Clue: Snirk the Goblin (9,10) and the Dwarves at Dwarvenhold (15,7) confirm that Rimefang (CR 13 White Dragon) hoards an ancient treasure chart and guards the Frozen Wind-Stele of Zephyrus inside his Glacial Chasm (17,10).
  • Target Locked: Boss 1: Rimefang.

# Step 3: Zephyrus's Revelation & Boss 2 (Loops 6–8)

  • The Unlock: Slaying Rimefang uncovers the Glacial Treasure Chart and unseals the Frozen Wind-Stele of Zephyrus, which teaches the party Djinni Zephyrus's True Name ("Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak") and the location of his physical Brass Lamp at the Aerie of the Four Winds (Hex 11, 12).
  • The South Clue: Zephyrus and the chart reveal the hidden coordinates of the Sunken Necropolis (Hex 12,16) in the southern desert dunes, where Mummy Lord Akh-en-Amon guards the ancient Inversion Tablets. Zephyrus offers 1 Wish (Necrotic Resistance) and a one-time Nimbus Cloud traversal (15m/hex in one move only) to help them reach the tomb!
  • Target Locked: Boss 2: Mummy Lord Akh-en-Amon.

# Step 4: The Alabaster Tablets & Unmasking Boss 3 (Loops 8–10)

  • The Unlock: Destroying Akh-en-Amon's Canopic Heart uncovers the Golden Alabaster Tablets.
  • The Shocking Revelation: The tablets prove the Angel and Devil traded bodies in the Arcanist's crucible before the loop, teach the Somatic Inversion Touch to heal the True Angel's fractured mind, and name the fiendish co-conspirator: Lord Ravana ("Ravana-Zul"), a feline Rakshasa!
  • The Epiphany:
  1. The Horned Fiend in the forest they fought in Loop 1 was NOT an evil devil—it was the TRUE ANGEL!
  2. Aurelius the Radiant in town is the TIGER-HEADED RAKSHASA!
  3. The tiger-headed deceiver has been playing them for fools to murder the Angel!
  • Target Locked: Boss 3: The Tiger-Headed Rakshasa (Lord Ravana).

# Step 5: Healing the True Angel, Creating the Time Loop & Boss 4 (Loops 9–11)

  • The Unlock: The party unmasks and defeats the Rakshasa, races north to Ash Grove (7,6), and performs the memorized Somatic Inversion Touch to heal the True Angel.
  • The Causal Bootstrap (Creating the Time Loop & Recontextualizing the Early Clues):
  • In this pivotal mid-campaign window—after defeating the Rakshasa (Boss 3) and restoring the True Angel, but BEFORE unchaining the Storm Giant (Boss 4)—the party and the True Angel work together to actually create the 12-hour time loop!
  • Rough Outline (05:30 AM → 05:59 AM):
  1. Together with the True Angel, the party jumps backward in time to 05:30 AM (before sunrise).
  2. At 05:45 AM, they descend in the pre-dawn fog onto The Commodore's beached caravel (Hex 5, 11) and steal the Chronocite Bone (knocking open his lockbox while coastal bandits grab the Winch Key in the commotion).
  3. Flying east at breakneck speed with the True Angel to beat the 06:00 AM chime, they come in too fast and crash straight into the western balcony of the Beregost Clocktower Belfry (Hex 8, 10), smashing the stone balustrade into rubble and jamming the bone into the Grand Escapement Gear at 05:59 AM—locking the clock at 05:59 AM for their 06:00 AM selves to be tasked with retrieving!
  • The Double "OH! THAT WAS US!" Epiphany:
  • "OH! That destroyed, rubbled Clocktower Belfry balcony we saw at 6:00 AM on Day 1—that was US crashing into the tower!"
  • "AND OH! That 5:45 AM theft the Commodore told us about earlier where flying thieves stole from his lockbox—that was US too!"
  • The West Clue: The restored True Angel also reveals why the Singing Devil's solar descent at the Western Sea Cliffs (6,8) is unopposed:

"West: free the storm-lord's herald on the reef, to bring the singing wings to grief! Lord Ravana grafted 4 Cursed Mind-Barnacles onto Valen Storm-Caller, the Huge Herald of Otheus aboard the Beached Caravel at Hex (5,11), so he could never sound the Storm-Conch to summon Tempest Lord Otheus. You must disarm the 09:30 AM Starfire fuse, shoot the ship's deck harpoons to haul the Huge Herald against the hull, and smash all 4 Cursed Barnacle Clusters on his body!"

  • Target Locked: Boss 4: Valen Storm-Caller, Huge Herald of Otheus (Summons Tempest Lord Otheus).

# Step 6: Summoning the Tempest & The 12-Hour Endgame Puzzle (Loops 11–13)

  • Harpoon-pull the Huge Herald of Otheus to the ship rail at (5,11) and smash all 4 Cursed Barnacle Clusters on his body so he blows the Abyssal Storm-Conch. Summoned from the deep trench, Tempest Lord Otheus pledges the 17:30 PM Category-5 Supercell Storm to deflect the solar beam and force the Singing Devil down to the Spire.
  • Combine all memorized knowledge ("Ravana-Zul", "Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak", the Somatic Inversion Touch, and Kaelen's Tachyonic Calibration Cipher) to solve and execute the 12-Hour Route Puzzle on the Final Loop!

# 13.2 The Bootstrap Paradox: Early Clues & How the Party + True Angel Create the Loop

# 1. The Two Early-Campaign Clues (Planted on Loop 0 / Loop 1, Recontextualized After Boss 3)

To make the mid-campaign time-loop creation land as an unforgettable "OH, THAT WAS US!" twist, the DM plants two seemingly incidental mysteries right at the start of the campaign:

  • Early Clue #1: The Destroyed, Rubbled Clocktower Belfry Balcony & The 05:59 AM Bone (Hex 8, 10):
  • Every loop at 05:59 AM / 06:00 AM when Artificer Bram Copperwheel tasks the party with unjamming the Clocktower's Grand Escapement Gear, the western stone balcony of the Clocktower Belfry is freshly smashed inward into rubble—with cracked masonry, black-and-silver scorch marks, and heavy impact gouges leading straight to the gear tooth where the Chronocite Bone is wedged at 05:59 AM.
  • On Loop 0 / Loop 1, Bram and the party assume some stray meteor or freak beast clipped the belfry balcony in the pre-dawn fog just before 06:00 AM.
  • Early Clue #2: The 05:45 AM Pre-Dawn Robbery of the Beached Caravel (Hex 5, 11 & Town Rumors):
  • Both in Beregost morning gossip (Tobias the Baker / Day 0 Rumor #5) and when the party inspects the Ship's Logbook aboard The Sea Maiden (Hex 5, 11), they learn of a chaotic 05:45 AM pre-dawn break-in in the coastal fog:
  • While local Silt-Gull bandits were lurking around the ship at 05:45 AM (stealing the Winch Crank-Key & Tuning Fork and fleeing to the Sea Caves at 4, 10), a frantic squad of intruders accompanied by a "hulking winged figure" dropped out of the fog onto the deck, snatched a strange pale fossilized bone from the captain's lockbox, and rocketed straight east toward Beregost!

# 2. Rough Outline of the Causal Bootstrap (Post-Rakshasa / Pre-Storm Giant)

After the party defeats the Rakshasa (Boss 3) and cures the True Angel at Ash Grove (Hex 7, 6), before calming the Herald of Otheus (Boss 4), the party and the True Angel enact the causal bootstrap:

  1. 05:30 AM — The Pre-Dawn Temporal Jump:
  • Working with the restored True Angel, the party travels back in time to 05:30 AM (30 minutes before the 06:00 AM Solstice sunrise).
  1. 05:45 AM — Stealing From the Beached Caravel (Hex 5, 11):
  • At 05:45 AM, they descend onto the Beached Caravel (Hex 5, 11) in the morning fog and steal the Chronocite Bone (the item they need to anchor the clocktower gear), causing the exact 05:45 AM commotion recorded in the Ship's Logbook and town gossip!
  1. 05:45–05:59 AM — Breakneck Flight, Aerial Discovery of the Burning Book & Crashing Into the Clocktower Belfry (Hex 8, 10):
  • ⭐ Aerial Breakthrough over Hex (7, 10) — The Tiny Fire & The Lost Burning Book: As the party and the True Angel hurtle eastbound across the western sky at 05:45 AM, they gaze down over the dark farmlands of Hex (7, 10). Down below, the field is not yet engulfed in the vast wildfire that chokes it during the day! Instead, they spot a tiny fire—a single isolated spark flickering in the twilight where their earlier selves dropped the Burning Book twenty minutes earlier on their way into town! From their aerial vantage point, they clearly spot the exact furrow beside the dry stone irrigation culvert where the book landed. Armed with this visual memory, the party can retrieve the Burning Book on any loop—an essential relic required to unseal the warded gates of the Spire of the Angel (Hex 6, 8)!
  • The Belfry Crash: Carried by the True Angel in a frantic sprint east to reach Beregost before 06:00 AM, they come in way too fast at 05:58–05:59 AM and crash straight through the stone balcony of the Clocktower Belfry, smashing it into the exact pile of rubble they saw on Loop 0!
  1. 05:59 AM — Jamming the Bone & Sticking the Clock at 05:59:
  • Scrambling out of the balcony rubble, they jam the Chronocite Bone into the Grand Escapement Gear at 05:59 AM, causing the clock and the time loop to lock at 05:59 AM—which their 06:00 AM selves are then tasked with climbing up and retrieving at the start of every loop!
  1. Why Only Memories & Level-Ups Persist:
  • Because the loop resets to 06:00 AM the moment their 06:00 AM selves pull the bone from the gears, only the party's memories and milestone level-ups carry across the reset boundary!

# 14.1 💀 The Sunken Necropolis of Akh-en-Amon (Hex 12, 16 via Waystation 14, 12)

  • Theme: Subterranean Desert Tomb & Suncophagus Vault
  • Recommended Level: Level 8–9 (Boss 2 Milestone)
  • Boss Threat: Mummy Lord (Akh-en-Amon) (CR 15)
  • Overview: Buried beneath centuries of shifting golden sands in the southern desert dunes (Hex 12, 16, guided via Zahir's Sandstone Sluice Waystation at Hex 14, 12) lies the subterranean crypt of Akh-en-Amon, high solar priest of the fallen dynasty. Sealed within its granite sarcophagus chamber are the ancient Inversion Swap Tablets that detail the forbidden soul-transference battery used by the corrupt arcanist.

# Strategic Relics & Campaign Breakthroughs

  • Golden Alabaster Inversion Tablets: Hieroglyphic stone tablets detailing soul-transference magic and the Somatic Inversion Touch; proves conclusively that the Angel and Devil had their physical forms swapped in the arcanist's battery.
  • Scarab Talisman of Sun-Warding: Wards against radiant damage (Resistance to Radiant) and allows reading ancient celestial hieroglyphs.

# Solstice Clockwork Timeline Hazards

  • 06:00 – 09:00 AM: Cool Morning Sands. Zahir's waystation at Hex (14, 12) and the necropolis entrance chute at Hex (12, 16) are stable and accessible via rope (DC 10 Athletics). Tomb interior is a cool 68°F shelter.
  • 09:00 – 12:00 PM: Thermal Sifting. Rising heat outside causes dune sand to pour into Room 1, creating quicksand sinkholes (DC 14 Dex save or restrained).
  • 12:00 – 15:00 PM: Midday Solar Seal. Entrance chute is choked with 15 feet of boiling 140°F sand. Entering requires digging (30 mins) or magical teleportation.
  • 15:00 – 18:00 PM: Necrotic Thermal Resonance. Suncophagus runes glow violet; all undead in the tomb gain +2 AC and regenerate 10 HP per round.

# Room-by-Room Layout (Labyrinthine Pyramid Floorplan)

  1. Room 1 (SW Vestibule): The Sifting Sand Descent & Twin Tunnel Branches
  • Description: A 40-foot sandstone shaft at the SW corner (A14–A15) drops into a shadowed vestibule centered on a 15-foot Quicksand Pit (C13–E15). Two passages branch out: the main North Processional Corridor (C9–D10) and a half-buried East Mason's Escape Crawlway (G15–I15).
  • Creatures: 2x Giant Dune Scorpion (SC1 at B11–C12, SC2 at D16–E17)
  • Hazard/Trap: Quicksand Pit (C13–E15): Sinks creatures 2 feet per round (DC 14 Str/Dex check to pull free).
  • Secrets/Loot: Cracked Bas-Relief (B9) in the North Tunnel depicts a solar priest splitting twin astral spirits with a crystal prism; spotting the hidden East Mason's Crawlway behind SC2 (DC 13 Perception) lets the party loop around into the east side of Room 2 and bypass the Tripwire Scythe Trap!
  1. Room 2 (NW U-Turn): The U-Shaped Hall of Canopic Guardians
  • Description: Flanked by jackal-headed pillars, this vaulted catacomb bends in a sharp inverted 'U': running North up the West Leg (B3–E8), turning 90 degrees East through the North Urn Turn (F2–G4), and turning 90 degrees South down the East Leg (H2–K8).
  • Creatures: 4x Dust Mephit Swarm (DM1 at C3, DM2 at I3), 2x Mummy Sentinels (MS1 at I7, MS2 at K7)
  • Hazard/Trap: West-Leg Tripwire Scythe Trap (B6–E6): DC 15 Perception to spot; DC 14 Dex save or takes 3d8 slashing and DC 13 Con save against mummy rot (bypassed via the Mason's Crawlway!).
  • Secrets/Loot: Canopic Urn of Breath (G2) at the top of the U-turn; plus a Secret Sliding Sarcophagus (L5–L6, DC 15 Investigation) in the east wall that opens a shortcut straight to Room 3's northern Tablet Dais—bypassing the long southern catacomb loop (I9 → I14 → M13)!
  1. Room 3 (Central S-to-N): Embalming Hall of the Solar Priest (Tablet Archive)
  • Description: A long astrological chamber running South-to-North (M4–Q15). Adventurers taking the main southern catacomb loop enter at M13 and fight Northward, while those taking the Secret Sarcophagus Shortcut emerge at M5 right beside the northern Tablet Dais!
  • Creatures: 1x Galeb Duhr Elder (GD1 at O10, animating boulders at N11 & Q11)
  • Hazard/Trap: Solar Rune Glyph Dais (O6–Q8): Stepping on the northern dais without speaking the solar glyph triggers a 4d10 radiant detonation (DC 15 Dex save for half).
  • Secrets/Loot: ⭐ Inversion Swap Tablets (O4–P4): Proves conclusively that the Angel and Devil swapped bodies and teaches the Somatic Inversion Touch! Behind the northern altar, a sealed portal opens into the NE Dogleg Ritual Causeway (R3–U4).
  1. Room 4 (East N-to-S): The Suncophagus Vault of Akh-en-Amon
  • Description: Hooking East and then South through the NE Ritual Causeway, the party enters the northern end of the Pharaoh's pillared vault (S5–X17) and battles Southward toward the golden sarcophagus at the southern wall.
  • Creatures: 1x Mummy Lord (Akh-en-Amon, BOSS at U13–V14) + 2x Sanctum Mummy Sentinels (MS3 at T9, MS4 at W9)
  • Hazard/Trap: Blazing Solar Ward (40 Temp HP, +2 AC; shattered by Sunburst Oil or Mirror-Aegis) & Sanctum Sentinels (vaporized by Scarab of Solar Resurgence).
  • Secrets/Loot: ⭐ Canopic Heart Sarcophagus Seal (U16–V16): Smashing the funerary heart seal inside the southern sarcophagus (AC 17, 50 HP) ends the Mummy Lord's rejuvenation for the current loop!

# 14.2 🐉 The Glacial Chasm & Rimefang's Frost Vault (Hex 17, 10)

  • Theme: Serpentine Sub-Zero Glacial Crevasse, Switchbacks & Ancient Dragon Lair
  • Recommended Level: Level 7 (Boss 1 Milestone)
  • Boss Threat: Adult White Dragon (Rimefang) (CR 13)
  • Overview: Perched on the high eastern peaks of Mount Rime lies a twisting, serpentine chasm of blue glacial ice. Rather than a linear tunnel, the cavern winds from a NW curving glissade (with a southern mountaineer's side-alcove), makes a sharp NE hairpin switchback south into a bifurcated crevasse (offering a choice between the direct Icicle Bridge or a southern climber's flanking ledge), spirals north up dwarven steps into an L-shaped Trophy Gallery, and descends southeast into the colossal Pillar-Vault where the Frozen Wind-Stele of Zephyrus (recording Djinni Zephyrus's True Name and his Brass Lamp's location at Hex 11, 12) is encased in ice.

# Strategic Relics & Campaign Breakthroughs

  • Rime-Anchor Harpoon: Adamantine whaling harpoon forged from meteor iron; when driven into Rimefang, pins the dragon to the ground, removing flight.
  • Djinni Zephyrus's True Name ("Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak"): Unsealing the Frozen Wind-Stele of Zephyrus in Rimefang's hoard teaches the party his True Name and 3-note wind cadence, allowing them to summon him at his physical Brass Lamp at Hex (11, 12) on any loop for 1 Elemental Wish + 1 One-Time Nimbus Cloud traversal (15 min/hex in one move only).
  • Drake-Bane Censer: Emits consecrated pine-pitch smoke that imposes disadvantage on dragon attacks and negates Frightful Presence.

# Solstice Clockwork Timeline Hazards

  • 06:00 – 08:30 AM: The Glacial Slumber. Rimefang is asleep atop the ice hoard. Stealth checks have advantage. Temperature is -15°F (requires cold gear or DC 12 Con save every hour).
  • 08:30 – 12:00 PM: The Morning Hunt. Rimefang takes flight circling the peak. The lair is guarded by the Winter Wolf pack. High altitude downdrafts.
  • 12:00 – 14:00 PM: Thermal Creep & Bridge Collapse. Valley heat begins warping the outer ice bridge. Crossing requires DC 15 Acrobatics or falls 80 ft into the crevasse.
  • 14:00 – 18:00 PM: Glacial Melting & Icicle Barrage. Ceiling melts and rains 10-foot razor icicles (DC 14 Dex save or 4d6 piercing/cold damage every 10 minutes).

# Room-by-Room Layout (Serpentine Switchback Floorplan)

  1. Room 1 (NW): The Curving Glissade & Southern Mountaineer's Alcove
  • Description: Descending from the NW cliff stairs (A2–A3), a steep chute of blue ice curves South-East (B3–F6). At the southern bend, a narrow frost-crack branches South into a dead-end Mountaineer's Alcove (B7–D10), while the main passage hooks North-East (H5–J5) and makes a 90-degree hairpin switchback South (I7–J10) into Room 2!
  • Creatures: 3x Giant Frost Spider (S1 at D3–E4, S2 in the South Alcove at B8–C9, S3 at the hairpin mouth F5–G6)
  • Hazard/Trap: Curving Ice Chute (B3–F6): Moving faster than half speed around the turn requires DC 13 Acrobatics or slides into the southern alcove stalagmites (2d6 bludgeoning).
  • Secrets/Loot: Frozen Mountaineer (C10 in the South Alcove): Clutches 3x Potions of Cold Resistance and Climber's Crampons (which grant automatic success on Room 2's Southern Flanking Ledge!).
  1. Room 2 (South-Central): The Bifurcated Crevasse — Bridge vs. Flanking Ledge
  • Description: Emerging from the northern hairpin tunnel into the south chasm (E11–M16), a 200-foot fissure offers Two Branching Routes East: Route A (North Icicle Bridge G12–J13) or Route B (Southern Climber's Ledge F15–K16).
  • Creatures: 2x Winter Wolf Pack Leader (W1 at K11–L12, W2 at K14–L15)
  • Hazard/Trap: Route A's Icicle Bridge shatters at 12:00 PM or after 20+ fire damage; Route B's Southern Ledge requires DC 12 Athletics (or automatic with Room 1's Crampons) and lets the party flank W2 from behind!
  • Secrets/Loot: Chasm Niche (H16 along Route B): Holds the frozen dragon hunter clutching the backup Drake-Bane Censer! From the east landing (M12), dwarven steps spiral 90 degrees North (N8–O11) into Room 3.
  1. Room 3 (NE Dogleg): The L-Shaped Frozen Trophy Gallery & Runestone Wing
  • Description: Entering from the southern spiral stair, this gallery branches into a quiet West Runestone Wing (L2–M5) and a dogleg North-to-East Gallery (N2–S7) that turns 90 degrees around frozen mammoth sculptures before descending South-East (R7–S9) into Room 4.
  • Creatures: 1x Abominable Yeti of Frostpeak (Y1 at Q3–S5, ambushing around the blind 90-degree NE corner)
  • Hazard/Trap: Corner Freezing Mist Geyser (O4–P5): Blasts 20-foot freezing steam across the L-bend every 2 rounds (DC 14 Con save or 3d6 cold and paralyzed 1 round).
  • Secrets/Loot: Dwarven Runestone (L3 in the West Wing): Teaches the pass-phrase 'Khazad-Mor' to pacify the sentinel at Hex (14,7).
  1. Room 4 (SE Sanctum — Colossal 60×60 ft Pillar Arena): The Glacial Pillar-Vault & Frozen Wind-Stele of Zephyrus
  • Description: Winding South-East from Room 3, the party emerges onto the elevated NW Grounding Plinth (N10–P10) overlooking a colossal 60×60 ft (12×12 square) subterranean glacier cathedral (M9–X20). Six massive dwarven granite-and-ice columns (Glacial Cover Pillars P1–P6 at O12, S12, O15, S15, O18, S18) rise from the floor, giving the party crucial three-quarters cover (+5 AC/Dex saves) and total cover against Rimefang's Cold Breath! At the back of the hoard stands the ice-encased Frozen Wind-Stele of Zephyrus (T14–U15) (Djinni Zephyrus himself is inside his Brass Lamp at Hex 11, 12; this tablet holds his True Name).
  • Creatures: 1x Adult White Dragon (Rimefang, BOSS at U13–W15)
  • Hazard/Trap: 6 Glacial Cover Pillars (P1–P6) & Permafrost Updrafts: Pillars provide 3/4 or Total Cover against Cold Breath (each pillar has AC 15, 60 HP). Rimefang hovers +80 ft regenerating 25 HP/round until grounded from the NW Plinth (N10–P10) with the Rime-Anchor Harpoon or Dwarven Ballistas.
  • Secrets/Loot: ⭐ Frozen Wind-Stele of Zephyrus (T14–U15): Dealing 50 fire damage or striking the ice block with the Rime-Anchor Harpoon shatters the glacial casing! Unsealing the ancient tablet reveals Djinni Zephyrus's True Name ("Zephyrus-Al-Mubarak") and 3-note wind cadence, plus the exact coordinates of his Brass Lamp buried at the Windswept Mesa (Hex 11, 12), where summoning him grants 1 Elemental Wish + 1 One-Time Nimbus Cloud (15 min/hex for one move only).

# 14.3 🎪 The Mirage Pavilion & Illusion Maze (Hex 10, 6)

  • Theme: Extradimensional Silk Palace & Illusion Labyrinth
  • Recommended Level: Level 10 (Boss 3 Milestone)
  • Boss Threat: Lord Ravana / 'Aurelius the Radiant' (CR 13)
  • Overview: Hidden within the jagged northern bluffs behind shimmering heat mirages sits the opulent extradimensional silk pavilion of Lord Ravana, the tiger-headed Rakshasa. While the valley swelters, Ravana reclines in magical luxury, sipping chilled wine and reviewing the corrupt arcanist's battery notes.

# Strategic Relics & Campaign Breakthroughs

  • The Arcanist's Resonance Ledger: Written in cipher; details the exact resonance frequencies of the Clocktower battery and proves Aurelius orchestrated the loop.
  • Blessed Quiver of Radiant Piercing: Arrows fired from this quiver ignore the Rakshasa's Limited Magic Immunity and deal an extra 2d8 radiant damage.
  • Inquisitive Monocle of Truth: Pierces the Rakshasa's Deva disguise and reveals his true tiger face, backwards hands, and illusions.

# Solstice Clockwork Timeline Hazards

  • 06:00 – 11:30 AM: The Grand Masquerade. Aurelius is away roaming the valley in Deva form deceiving travelers. Pavilion is sealed by a DC 20 illusion veil.
  • 12:00 – 15:30 PM: The Extradimensional Siesta. Ravana rests inside the pavilion with his charmed retinue. The illusion maze is fully active.
  • 15:30 – 17:00 PM: Contingency Evacuation. Ravana packs the pavilion and teleports toward the clocktower to oversee the sunset cataclysm.
  • 17:00 – 18:00 PM: Abandoned Illusion Husk. The pavilion collapses into an arcane vortex, dealing 8d8 force damage to anyone inside.

# Room-by-Room Layout (The Four Trial Illusions)

  1. Room 1 (Illusion #1 — The Time-Loop Restart Mirage): The Shimmering Mirage Boundary
  • Description: Stepping through the wavering silk entrance plunges the party into Illusion #1: The Phantom Dawn Reset! Read the 06:00 AM Dawn Monologue verbatim to trick the players into believing the time loop just restarted back at the Clocktower balcony.
  • Creatures: 2x Briarwood Displacer Beast (CR 3)
  • Hazard/Trap: The Phantom Dawn Reset: Spot any of the 5 Matrix Glitches (guard casts no shadow, honey-bun tastes like dry silk & sand, velvet balcony, sun moving west-to-east, missing Scribe Vane) and pass a DC 16 Investigation/Wisdom check (or use the Monocle of Truth) to shatter the fake morning sky.
  • Secrets/Loot: Silk Banner: Embroidered with a tiger devouring a fallen sun (can also be draped over Room 2's mirrors to block reflections!).
  1. Room 2 (Illusion #2 — Freestanding Mirrors & Unsuspected 'Evil Twins'): Gallery of Freestanding Palace Mirrors
  • Description: A wide, sunlit silk-draped gallery (B10–N17) featuring two ornate, freestanding full-length gilded dressing mirrors positioned in the open floor (Mirror A at F13 facing South, and Mirror B at J14 facing North) with generous 10-to-15-foot walkways all around them. Do not telegraph that anything is evil or magical about the mirrors—they look like ordinary, normal palace mirrors reflecting the room until someone carelessly steps directly in front of the glass!
  • Creatures: 2x Mirror "Evil Twin" (CR 13, 180 HP — Triggers Only If a PC Walks Directly In Front of a Mirror!)
  • Hazard/Trap: Unsuspected Mirror Sightlines (F14–F16 & J11–J13): Players have plenty of room to walk around the backs and sides of both freestanding mirrors. Only if a PC steps directly across the 15-ft frontal reflection zone of Mirror A (F14–F16) or Mirror B (J11–J13)—or peers straight into the glass—do they find out the hard way as their reflection smiles with backwards hands and steps out as a lethal CR 13 Evil Twin! Once discovered, the party can walk around the mirrors' backs/sides, drape a cloak over them from the side, or shatter a mirror frame from behind (AC 13, 20 HP—destroying a mirror immediately shatters its Evil Twin!).
  • Secrets/Loot: Rosewood Vanity Table (M10, in the safe NE corner behind the mirrors): Holds a velvet-lined box containing a backup Inquisitive Monocle of Truth.
  1. Room 3 (Illusion #3 — The Fake Boss Defeat Trick): The Opulent Silk Divan & Feasting Salon
  • Description: Plush crimson velvet carpets and banquet tables where "Lord Ravana" lounges on a gilded divan flanked by charmed guards and engages the party in a dramatic "Boss Battle."
  • Creatures: 1x Illusory Lord Ravana (CR 7 Mirage Decoy, 95 HP, AC 16) + 4x Charmed Elite Bodyguards (CR 4)
  • Hazard/Trap: The False Boss Victory Ruse: Engineered to bait the party into burning their highest-level spell slots and smites! When reduced to 0 HP, this fake Ravana gasps dramatically and melts into laughing golden sand and purple smoke as the Real Lord Ravana mocks them from behind the illusory northern wall (R9–S9)! Pierce the false wall (DC 15 Investigation or Monocle of Truth) to enter Room 4.
  • Secrets/Loot: Silver Wine Flagon (P12): Pours unpoisoned chilled Elverquisst wine (+10 Temp HP per cup, 1/day).
  1. Room 4 (Illusion #4 — Real Lord Ravana & 'Table Talk = Advantage' Mind Reading): The Hall of Three Obsidian Mirrors
  • Description: Behind the false wall lies the true inner sanctum ringed by three 15-foot Obsidian Mirrors (M1, M2, M3) and the Ash Grove Delirium Conduit (U7–U8), guarded by the Real Lord Ravana (CR 13, 210 HP, AC 18).
  • Creatures: 1x Real Lord Ravana / 'Aurelius' (CR 13 True Boss)
  • Hazard/Trap: Telepathic Table-Talk Mind Reading ("Table Talk = Advantage!"): In Room 4, any out-of-character tactical table talk spoken aloud by the players at the table is heard telepathically by Ravana—granting him Advantage on saves/defense against that declared attack (imposing Disadvantage on the attack roll) AND Advantage on his counterattack! Players must coordinate via silent hand gestures, written notes, cryptic in-character speech, or the Circlet of Mind Sanctity (Hex 9,7), while shattering his 3 Obsidian Mirrors (AC 15, 30 HP).
  • Secrets/Loot: ⭐ Compelled Confession & The Resonance Ledger: Upon true defeat in Room 4, infernal law compels Ravana to speak his True Name ("Ravana-Zul"), shattering the Delirium Hex on the True Angel at Hex (7,6) and confessing that he grafted Cursed Mind-Barnacles onto the Herald of Otheus at Hex (5,11)!

# 14.4 ⚓ The Beached Caravel — Harpoon-Pull Duel with the Huge Herald of Otheus (Hex 5, 11)

  • Theme: Beached War Galleon, Harpoon-Pull Ship-Deck Lightning Arena, & Summoning of Tempest Lord Otheus
  • Recommended Level: Level 11 (Boss 4 Milestone)
  • Boss Threat: Valen Storm-Caller, The Huge Herald of Otheus (CR 13, 230 HP, AC 18 — Harpoon-Pull Ship-Deck Duel) → Summons Tempest Lord Otheus
  • Overview: Stranded at a 15-degree list in the treacherous western tidal flats lies The Sea Maiden, an ancient 60-gun war caravel. Held captive on the wreck is Valen Storm-Caller, the Huge 25-foot-tall Herald of Otheus, whom Lord Ravana maddened by grafting 4 Clusters of Cursed Mind-Barnacles directly onto his body! At 09:30 AM, raiders light a 15-minute Starfire powder fuse in the lower hold; when the party disarms the bomb and ascends to the top of the main ship deck, the Huge Herald stands 35 feet outside the ship in the deep surf (out of melee reach) whacking onto the deck while Sahuagin guard the ship's two Heavy Whaling Harpoon-Launchers (HP1 & HP2)! Melee characters must fight to a Harpoon-Launcher, aim it, and shoot a chained harpoon into the Herald to winch him right up against the ship rail for 1 round so the party can smash the 4 Cursed Barnacle Clusters on his body before he snaps the chain and retreats! Once all 4 barnacles on the Herald are destroyed, he regains his senses and blows his Abyssal Storm-Conch to summon the massive Storm Giant, Tempest Lord Otheus, for the 17:30 PM Supercell Storm-Cloud!

# Strategic Relics & Campaign Breakthroughs

  • The Stolen Relic Box of the Sea Maiden: Recovered from the Raider Sea Caves (Hex 4, 10). Contains:
  1. The Abyssal Winch Crank-Key: 3-foot adamantine spindle key that slots into the caravel's capstan (J6) to stabilize the 15-degree listing ship deck (removing Difficult Terrain) AND power the mechanized Harpoon Winches (allowing harpoons at N4/N8 to be aimed, fired, and reeled in as a Bonus Action with Advantage!).
  2. The Brass Tidal Tuning Fork: Resonant harmonic fork (note of F-sharp) that dampens Crashing Broadside Waves on the ship deck and loosens the 4 Cursed Barnacle Clusters on the Huge Herald's body (lowering their AC from 16 to 13).
  3. Forged Town Hall Promissory Chit: Proof of a 500 gp bounty from a hooded emissary (the disguised Rakshasa) to scuttle the caravel.
  • Grounding Rod of the Deep Trench (Hex 4, 11): Planted into the wooden ship deck at the mainmast (M6), it absorbs all Storm-Conducting Wet Plank chain-lightning across the ship and channels a 10d8 Lightning surge straight down the iron harpoon cable into the Huge Herald—instantly blasting off one of the 4 Cursed Barnacle Clusters on his chest!
  • Abyssal Storm-Conch: Sounded by the Herald of Otheus once all 4 Cursed Barnacle Clusters on his body are destroyed, summoning the colossal Tempest Lord Otheus to unleash the 17:30 PM Category-5 Supercell Storm-Cloud!
  • The Mariner's Astrolabe: +2 to naval/aquatic checks and resistance to pressure damage.

# Solstice Clockwork Timeline Hazards

  • 06:00 – 09:30 AM: Morning Low Tide. The caravel is surrounded by damp sand flats; the Herald of Otheus is bound in shock-chains with 4 Cursed Barnacle Clusters on his body while raiders prepare the powder hold.
  • 09:30 – 09:45 AM: 🔥 STARFIRE FUSE BURNING! Raiders light the 15-minute fuse to 12 barrels of starfire powder. Party has 15 minutes to reach the gun deck and disarm!
  • 09:45 AM: 💥 POWDER EXPLOSION & WRECKAGE AFTERMATH (If Not Disarmed). Deals 100d6 fire damage, blowing The Sea Maiden in half and killing the captive Herald. If the party arrives after 09:45 AM, they find burning oak ribs and the scorched Captain's Logbook washed ashore alongside dying Bosun Cord—revealing the 05:45 AM double-robbery (winged thieves took the pale Chronocite Bone; Silt-Gull bandits took the Winch Key to Hex 4, 10) and the 09:30 AM Starfire fuse attack!
  • 10:00 AM+ (If Rescued): ⚡ BOSS 4 HARPOON-PULL SHIP-DECK DUEL: The storm-frenzied Huge Herald of Otheus (CR 13, 230 HP, AC 18) wades into the foaming surf 35 ft outside the ship; the party fights Sahuagin on top of the deck to fire the Harpoon-Launchers (HP1/HP2), pulling him against the rail to smash the 4 Cursed Barnacle Clusters on his body!

# Room-by-Room Layout

  1. Room 1: Flooded Gun Deck & Starfire Powder Hold
  • Description: Knee-deep seawater sloshes across cannonballs and shattered crates. At the far bulkhead, a hissing white-hot Starfire fuse burns down toward 12 powder kegs!
  • Creatures: 1x Sahuagin Baron & Raider Demolitionists
  • Hazard/Trap: 🔥 Ticking Fuse (09:30–09:45 AM): Requires DC 15 Sleight of Hand or water/cold spell to extinguish before detonation.
  • Secrets/Loot: Captain's Logbook in the chart locker reveals the 05:45 AM theft of the Chronocite Bone by winged intruders and the Winch Key theft to Hex (4, 10).
  1. Room 2: Top of the Main Ship Deck — Shoot Harpoons to Pull the Huge Herald Into the Ship & Target His 4 Barnacles!
  • Description: Ascending to the top of the open wooden weather deck of The Sea Maiden (Cols H–P, Rows 3–9), the party confronts Valen Storm-Caller, the Huge 25-foot-tall Herald of Otheus! By default, the Huge Herald stands 35 feet outside the ship in the deep ocean surf (Cols R–T, Rows 5–7, out of melee reach) while Sahuagin deck-guards (SD1 at L4, SD2 at L8) block the ship's two Heavy Whaling Harpoon-Launchers (HP1 at N4 & HP2 at N8). Melee characters must fight to a Harpoon-Launcher, aim it, and shoot a chained harpoon into the Herald to pull him right up against the ship's railing (Cols O–Q) so the party can smash the 4 Cursed Mind-Barnacle Clusters on the Herald himself before he snaps the chain and retreats back into the surf!
  • Creatures: 1x The Huge Herald of Otheus (CR 13, 230 HP, AC 18 — Starts 35 ft Outside Ship at R5–T7; Harpoon Pulls Him to O5–Q7; 4 Targetable Barnacles on Him: AC 16 [13 w/ Tuning Fork], 55 HP each) + 2x Sahuagin Harpoon-Guards (SD1 at L4, SD2 at L8)
  • Hazard/Trap: The 3-Step Harpoon-Pull Cycle, Pitching Deck & Wet-Plank Lightning: (1) Fight Sahuagin on the pitching deck to reach HP1 (N4) or HP2 (N8); (2) Aim & shoot a harpoon (Action: Attack vs AC 15 or DC 14 Athletics; Bonus Action w/ Advantage if the Abyssal Winch Key from Hex 4,10 is slotted at Capstan J6) to drag the Herald to the starboard rail (O5–Q7) for 1 round of melee with Advantage against his 4 Barnacles; (3) After 1 round (or when 1 Barnacle breaks), he snaps the cable and retreats back to R5–T7!
  • Secrets/Loot: ⭐ Targeting the 4 Barnacles on the Herald & Summoning Tempest Lord Otheus: Planting the Grounding Rod (Hex 4,11) at Mast M6 absorbs wet-plank lightning and sends a 10d8 surge down the harpoon cable to instantly pop 1 Barnacle Cluster on the Herald's chest! Once all 4 Cursed Barnacle Clusters on the Huge Herald himself are destroyed, he regains his senses and blows his Abyssal Storm-Conch to summon Tempest Lord Otheus for the 17:30 PM Supercell Storm-Cloud!

# 14.4.1 The Herald of Otheus & The Beached Caravel Narrative Arc

Valen Storm-Caller, the Herald of Otheus, chained aboard the wrecked caravel The Sea Maiden (Hex 5, 11), represents the tempestuous maritime anchor of the western campaign—and holds Early Recontextualization Clue #2:

  • The Barnacle-Maddened Captive: Chained to the mainmast of the listing caravel, Valen Storm-Caller has 4 Clusters of Cursed Mind-Barnacles attached to his neck and bronze storm-scale armor by Lord Ravana (the Rakshasa), driving him into a violent lightning frenzy so he attacks anyone who frees him!
  • The Predawn Double-Robbery (05:45 AM — Early Bootstrap Clue #2): Fifteen minutes before the 06:00 AM reset, two things happened in the sea mist at 05:45 AM:
  1. The Winged Intruders & The Stolen Chronocite Bone: A frantic squad of intruders accompanied by a "hulking winged figure" dropped out of the pre-dawn fog at 05:45 AM, broke open the captain's heavy iron lockbox, stole a strange pale fossilized bone (the Chronocite Bone) dredged up from the trench, and rocketed straight east toward Beregost at breakneck speed! (After defeating the Rakshasa, the players realize: "Oh! That 05:45 AM theft of the bone from the caravel—that was US and the True Angel after jumping back to 05:30 AM!")
  2. The Opportunistic Silt-Gull Bandits: In the 05:45 AM confusion, coastal Silt-Gull bandits slipped aboard and fled to the Raider Sea Caves (Hex 4, 10) with the mahogany Relic Box of the Sea Maiden (holding the Abyssal Winch Crank-Key & Brass Tidal Tuning Fork).
  • The Ship-Deck Harpoon Dilemma: Without the Abyssal Winch Crank-Key & Brass Tidal Tuning Fork (Hex 4, 10) and the Grounding Rod of the Deep Trench (Hex 4, 11), the 15-degree listing wooden deck of The Sea Maiden is slick Difficult Terrain that conducts 2d8 splash lightning across the wet planks while the Huge Herald stands 35 ft outside in the surf!
  • The Desperate Countdown: At 09:30 AM, raiders and a Sahuagin Baron light a 15-minute Starfire powder fuse in the flooded lower gun deck. At 09:45 AM, the caravel explodes unless the fuse is cut! Once the party disarms the bomb, shoots the Deck Harpoons (HP1/HP2) to pull the Huge Herald against the ship rail, and smashes all 4 Cursed Barnacle Clusters on his body, he calms down and blows his Abyssal Storm-Conch to summon Tempest Lord Otheus!

# 14.4.2 The Predawn Bandit Robbery & The Stolen Relic Box (Hex 4, 10 - Raider Sea Caves)

  • Location: Hex (4, 10) Raider Sea Caves (Wave-hollowed chalk cliffs, 1 hex northwest of the caravel).
  • Access Window: 06:00 – 10:00 AM (Accessible on foot across exposed mud flats during low tide). After 10:30 AM, the rising storm tides flood the cave mouths with 15 feet of scalding water, drowning anyone inside.
  • The Culprits: The Silt-Gull Bandits, led by Captain "Shark-Tooth" Bloodfin (CR 3 Bandit Captain) and Prophet Joshua (CR 2 Cult Fanatic / Apostate Tide-Caller).
  • The Ritual Scene (06:30 – 08:30 AM):
  • Deep within the chalk cavern, Prophet Joshua stands atop a barnacle-crusted altar over the open Gilded Relic Box.
  • In his hand, he strikes the Brass Tidal Tuning Fork against the stone. Turquoise ripples shimmer across the flooded floor, sending low harmonic vibrations reverberating out into the ocean trench.
  • Joshua chants: "Rise, daughters of the deep! Hear the tone of the sunken bell! Scuttle the warship, claim the iron, and the gold of Beregost is ours!"
  • Tactical Encounter (CR 3):
  • 1x Prophet Joshua (Cult Fanatic; uses Tidal Chime as an action: 15-ft cone, DC 12 Con save or 2d8 thunder damage and pushed 10 ft).
  • 4x Silt-Gull Raiders (Bandits with poisoned scimitars, +4 to hit, 1d6+2 slashing + 1d6 poison).
  • Investigation & Recovery:
  • Defeating or intimidating Joshua (DC 13 Intimidation) recovers the intact Relic Box, containing the Abyssal Winch Crank-Key, the Brass Tidal Tuning Fork, and a forged Town Hall promissory note sealed by a hooded deceiver.
  • Using the Crank-Key & Tuning Fork aboard the Beached Caravel at Hex (5, 11) stabilizes the pitching ship deck (removing Difficult Terrain), powers the Deck Harpoon winches (Bonus Action fire/pull w/ Advantage), and loosens the 4 Cursed Mind-Barnacles on the Huge Herald's body (AC 16 → 13)!

# 14.4.3 The Mechanics of the Rising Storm Tides (The Triple Convergence)

Why do the violent, scalding storm tides roll in from the west? The phenomenon is driven by three intersecting metaphysical and physical forces:

flowchart TD
    Gravity["1. Planar Gravitational Pull
    Solar battery pulls sun downward;
    unnatural tidal force draws Sea of Swords inland"] --> Surge["THE SCALDING STORM TIDES (11:30 - 17:30)
    15-to-25 ft boiling storm surge (120°F - 150°F)"]
    Tuning["2. The Stolen Tuning Fork
    Prophet Joshua strikes brass fork in Hex 4,10;
    acoustic shockwaves vibrate continental shelf"] --> Surge
    Otheus["3. The Herald's Storm-Frenzy
    Barnacle-maddened Herald of Otheus
    discharges wild lightning into the reef;
    superheated steam boils ocean outward"] --> Surge
    Surge --> Climax["17:30 Climax: Otheus Summoned
    Calmed Herald blows Abyssal Storm-Conch;
    Tempest Lord Otheus unleashes Category-5 Supercell!"]
  1. Convergence Factor 1: The Planar Gravitational Warp: The Arcanist's celestial battery drags the sun down toward the town belfry. This unnatural celestial displacement generates an intense gravitational warp on the Sea of Swords, forcing a premature, violent tidal surge hours ahead of normal lunar cycles.
  2. Convergence Factor 2: The Tuning Fork's Resonant Shockwave: Prophet Joshua striking the brass tuning fork inside the Raider Sea Caves excites the natural acoustic frequency of the shallow shelf trench. The sound reverberates through underwater caverns, generating a continuous tidal bore.
  3. Convergence Factor 3: The Herald's Electrical Agony: Chained to the caravel's mainmast, the barnacle-maddened Herald of Otheus discharges wild arcs of tempest lightning into the iron ballast chains and shallow reef, superheating the seawater into boiling steam and driving a foaming storm surge toward the coast!
  4. Environmental Stages of the Tide:
  • 06:00 – 08:30 AM (Low Tide / Damp Flats): Water receded 300 yards. Damp grey sand, exposed mud flats, easily crossed on foot (1 hour per hex).
  • 09:00 – 10:30 AM (The First Surge / Frothing Bore): A 4-foot wall of white foam rolls inland. Water crackles with divine static (harmless sparks on metal).
  • 11:00 AM – 14:00 PM (The Scalding Storm Tide / 120°F–140°F): The ocean rushes back with 15-foot storm swells. Water is scalding hot (deals 1d6 fire damage per round of immersion without resistance). Foot travel across the flats is impossible.
  • 15:00 – 17:15 PM (The Boiling Tempest / 150°F+): 25-foot boiling tidal waves smash against the chalk cliffs. Steam clouds billow 200 feet into the air.
  • 17:30 PM (The Supercell Climax): Summoned by the calmed Herald's Abyssal Storm-Conch, Tempest Lord Otheus ascends through the boiling surf and directs the vast oceanic energy upward into the atmosphere, creating the Category-5 Supercell Thunderstorm that shields Beregost and saves the valley!
